about: teuf-teuf parts and contact schema (plan 3, Olog), the [substitute] operation, asserts for invariants 1-3 (+7) with results, foraged-item evidence and handmade records. Written by sim.py.

input_force.note: hands pinned to the stone's rear face at the same world height in every trial; the push clock tau runs 0-7 s in drag, rollers and wheel; the counter-check replays the wheel trial's input for tau 0-1.6

period.note: shown as a demonstration, no date on screen

contacts.law: stick-slip: static/kinetic friction, body as spring
rear foot re-plants after every slip

failure_mode.note: nine lurches of 0.133 m; the stone thinks it over between them

mechanisms.name: rollers

period.note: no date; roller-to-wheel lineage is contested (register R5)

parts: log D (spare, set down in front)

contacts.law: no slip: log centre at v/2, rotation (v/2)/R
lowest outline point tangent to the ground

failure_mode.event: logs drift back at v/2 and fall out behind; the load waits while a log is carried

mechanisms.name: wheel and axle

period.note: Copper Age / Baden culture (Commons categories of the wheel photograph); no number shown on screen

parts: wheel image: GrabCut cutout of the Ljubljana Marshes wheel photograph (foraged)

contacts.law: axle turns in a bearing notch under the platform, held by the hold-down beam; the wheel is fixed to its axle (square hole, as in the Ljubljana wheel)
no slip: theta = dx/R, wheel stays under the load
step <= 0.75 m, so cadence must rise

failure_mode.event: none in the window; the pusher's walking becomes the limit

mechanisms.name: counter-check: wheels without the axle contact
mechanisms.substitution: remove contact kind 'axle' only (pin pulled, beam lifts away); same cart, same push input

contacts.law: loose: wheel centre at v/2 under the platform

substitute.operation: Mechanism x Load -> Mechanism' x Load (moving_parts and contacts swapped; load, input force, frame, window kept)
substitute.counterexample: wheels without the axle contact behave as rollers: rear wheel drops out, load stops at 0.9481 m

push_window_tau_s.counter: tau 0-1.6 of the wheel trial's input

invariant_3_continuity.wide_and_closeup_share_state: one sim state per instant; cam B frames (16.21-18.79 s) carry the same load record

ik_reach_excess_px.note: max distance by which a foot/hand target exceeds the test-shot puppet's limb lengths (Puppet: thigh 63s, shin 61s, arms 48s+46s; P s=1.2, C s=1.15). The large C value is the shove follow-through (13.04 s) and seated leg extensions; the animator's ik2 clamps, so residuals there are expected and reported in animation.json

layout_warning.why: with x0 = 330 and the approved 250 px stone, the rear face is at x 80 at 0 m; the pusher's hip is 134 px behind his hands (40 deg lean), so at 0 m his hip sits at x ~ -54 and his rear foot near -140. During the whole drag (0-1.2 m) and the first second of every later trial he is half cropped at frame left. kf-1 had the same issue less badly (smaller figures).
options: accept the crop (the reference frieze crops animals at the edges)
the director moves x0 to ~430 (8 m then reaches 1230; ticks and ghosts move with it)
narrow the stone to ~180 px (breaks the approved test-shot stone)

deviations_from_plan: Rollers push clock: tau 2.2 falls at 16.95 s (not 16.2) so that, as in the approved test shot, log A is squeezed out inside the close-up (release 16.25, stop 16.84, caption 17.2 = +0.36 s). tau 0-2.2 -> 14.0-16.95, tau 2.2-4.8 -> 16.95-21.0 (the wait), tau 4.8-7.0 -> 21.0-23.0.
Resets are declared cuts at 12.75 (scratch wipe 12.5-12.75), 25.0 (wipe 24.75-25.0) and 34.0 (dissolve 34.0-34.25); camera cuts at 16.2 and 18.8. Load x is continuous everywhere else.
Only the pusher walks in (0-3.4 s); the carrier stands at the rope from the start (walking in from either edge would need > 2 m/s with a 0.75 m step).
Log D is a fourth, spare log lying at x 700 from the rollers reset; the carrier walks to it, faces left, carries it back and sets it 30 px ahead of the waiting stone (19.70), steps clear by 22.0.

Log A comes to rest 191 px behind the stone's rear edge (review fix), between the pusher's feet: it rolls under his lead foot, which lifts 58 px and re-plants ahead of the log (contact-driven, #33). This spot also keeps A clear of the cart's rear wheel at 0 m (4 px gap) and of the fallen wheel in shot 6.
Counter-check caption is caused by the platform hitting the ground (36.30 -> 36.6, +0.30 s); the pin pull (34.6) is its own beat (click). Wheel drop 36.07, stop 36.83 at 0.95 m.

In profile the cart shows two wheels, each on its own axle in bearings under the platform; the 'axle' contact is held by one hold-down beam with a pin at the platform's rear end, which the pusher pulls.
Shot 6: the pusher sits on the forgotten log A (39.6); that contact is the impulse for its one last rock and tok (#41: no motion without a sim event).
